rows.text: It’s easy to report online at www.mhra.gov.uk/yellowcard
REPORT OF SUSPECTED ADVERSE DRUG REACTIONS

If you suspect an adverse reaction may be related to one or more drugs/vaccines/complementary remedies, please complete this Yellow Card. See ‘Adverse reactions to drugs’ section in the British National Formulary (BNF) or www.mhra.gov.uk/yellowcard for guidance. Do not be put off reporting because some details are not known.

rows.text: Information on adverse drug reactions received by the MHRA can be downloaded at www.mhra.gov.uk/daps Stay up‐to‐date on the latest advice for the safe use of medicines with our monthly bulletin Drug Safety Update at www.mhra.gov.uk/drugsafetyupdate
Please attach additional pages if necessary. Send to: FREEPOST YELLOW CARD (no other address details required)
Please use the Yellow Card Scheme to tell us about:
• All suspected adverse drug reactions for new medicines ‐ identified by the black triangle ▼ symbol
• All suspected adverse drug reactions occurring in children, even if a medicine has been used off‐label
• All serious* suspected adverse drug reactions for established vaccines and medicines, including unlicensed medicines, herbal remedies, and medicines used off‐label
• All medication errors that result in an adverse reaction
*Reactions which are fatal, life‐threatening, a congenital abnormality, disabling or incapacitating, result in or prolong hospitalisation, or medically significant are considered serious.
If you are unsure, please report anyway
• Contact the Yellow Card Information Service on Freephone 0800 731 6789
• Visit the Yellow Card website – www.mhra.gov.uk/yellowcard

normalization_notes: Both source pages are retained, including the reverse mailing face, fold labels and guidance. One complete two-page form, not a page fragment.

Government logo artwork excluded. All substantive prose, punctuation, choices, contact URLs and public-service telephone text retained; whitespace/line wrapping normalized. Static official contacts are source instructions, not synthetic contacts.

Twenty-eight logical columns retain four-part patient details, seven-column medicine tables (three suspected rows and four other-drug rows), side-by-side reaction/outcome and reporter/clinician sections. No dropdowns or essential rowspans occur in this source.

Printed slash-delimited M / F, Y / N and Yes / No choices are represented by exclusive checkbox groups. Original slash-delimited text remains in the same label cell above each normalized group; options are not removed. Reverse-side bullet marks are encoded as Unicode bullets instead of the PDF font-specific glyph.

Serious-reaction categories retain their source left/right grouping. The source has five tickboxes and a separate Medically significant; please give details: writing line, not a sixth printed tickbox. The five boxes remain two spatial groups with a common source instruction; the written-details target remains separate.

Repeated medicine-row schema keys 1-3 and 1-4 denote source row order, not added visible labels. Name and Professional Address: remains one multi-line source field, not invented separate controls. Only the reporter has a source signature field.

Inactive medicine and significance fields retain explicit synthetic annotation-only N/A values under the nonblank text-gold contract. No real prescription, clinician identity or professional certificate is constructed.
Historical guidance is not current medical advice.
